{"id": "fb70bfb0-392a-41e5-af1a-7757d30d570f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "An Application Load Balancer (ALB) works at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and routes on request content. A Network Load Balancer (NLB) works at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS) and routes on connection data, with very high throughput and low latency.

| | **ALB** | **NLB** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, TLS |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query strings, HTTP method, source IP | Port and protocol only |
| **Performance** | Good, but it inspects each request, so latency is higher | Millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, and it handles sudden traffic spikes well |
| **IP addressing** | Dynamic IPs, so you use its DNS name | One static IP per Availability Zone, and you can attach Elastic IPs |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, and ALBs (an ALB can be an NLB target) |
| **Client IP** | Passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserved at the network level (for instance targets) |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS, with SNI and multiple certificates | Terminates or passes through TLS |
| **Authentication** | Built-in OIDC and Cognito authentication | None |
| **WAF** | Supported | Not supported |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023) |
| **PrivateLink** | Not a PrivateLink endpoint service source | Can front a VPC endpoint service |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You're serving web apps, REST APIs, or microservices and need path-based or host-based routing.
- You want features such as redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, authentication, or WAF.
- You're running containers (ECS or EKS) and want several services behind one load balancer.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency.
- You're handling non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT, VoIP, or custom TCP/UDP.
- Clients need static or allow-listable IP addresses.
- You're exposing a service through AWS PrivateLink.

**Using both:** A common pattern is an NLB in front of an ALB. This gives you static IPs and PrivateLink support from the NLB, plus Layer 7 routing from the ALB.

I can also look at the load balancers in your account, for example to see which ones you have and how they're configured.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
